title: Why Not to Buy an Extended Car Warranty (Scam)
summary: Mechanic argues extended car warranties mostly benefit the salesperson's commission, except on unreliable luxury brands.

assertions.quote: the Commission to the sales guy is almost 50% of what you're paying for the entire insurance policy

verdicts.note: Commissions on F&I add-ons including warranties are known to be high, often cited in the 40-60% range, but it varies by company and role.

assertions.quote: guess who decides what's covered and what isn't the company itself

verdicts.note: Warranty administrators interpret their own contracts, a well-documented source of coverage disputes.

assertions.quote: the only person that could really comprehend this policy would be a lawyer / mechanic

verdicts.note: Contracts do carry dense exclusions and legal language, though claiming only a lawyer-mechanic could parse one overstates it.

assertions.quote: the company didn't exist anymore, they'd gone bankrupt

verdicts.note: Third-party service contract administrators have failed before, leaving contract holders without recourse, though it is not the typical outcome.

assertions.quote: you're better off looking at the money that it costs for the extended warranty, just put that in the bank
they ended up getting five or six times the amount of work done that they paid for the policy on those cars

verdicts.note: Luxury and European models do have above-average repair frequency and cost, but whether payouts exceed price is anecdotal and plan-dependent.
